title: Advanced Combustion via Microgravity Experiments Electric-Field Effects on Laminar Diffusion Flames
platform: International Space Station (ISS), Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR), ACME
summary: Methane and ethylene laminar diffusion flames subjected to high-voltage electric fields (up to 10 kV) with coflow and gas-jet burners in the CIR aboard the ISS in microgravity to investigate ion-driven convection, flame stability, and soot dynamics.

tests.notes: First round of tests with coflow burner. Test date 2018-03-14 (GMT day 18073). Electrode mesh polarity: negative. Fuel bottle 100% CH4, burned at 100% CH4. Flames ignited that day: 10 (count not split by fuel concentration). O2 21% (derived): the PSI-22 approach says the coflow burner surrounds the fuel jet with a weak synthetic air flow; 21% is the nominal O2 of air. Pressure is not given in the summary table or the investigation page; assumed nominal 101.3 kPa. Table note: fuel concentration (diluted with N2 by volume) was varied between tests, typically matched the bottle, and the list only accounts for flames ignited.
